business.description: Mangalam Organics Limited is a pioneer in pine chemistry and a leading manufacturer of terpene and resin derivatives. The company manufactures camphor, dipentene, sodium acetate, isobornyl acetate, isoborneol, terpene phenolic resin, alkyl phenolic resin, and resin esters, serving industrial, religious, personal care, and household applications.

outlook.statement: The international camphor market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 7.2% during 2026-2032, driven by increasing demand across diverse applications. The trend towards herbal and ayurvedic products, especially in pharmaceutical and personal care industries, has fueled demand for natural camphor. The Indian chemical industry remains a critical pillar of the nation's industrial growth story, with India well-positioned to emerge as a leading manufacturing hub for specialty chemicals and value-added products.

Strategic priorities remain clear: strengthening operational excellence, expanding product portfolio, investing in innovation, deepening customer relationships and embedding sustainability into every aspect of business. The company intends to focus on manufacturing and marketing high quality intermediate products to international customers: Camphene for paint, resin and fragrance applications; Isobornyl Acetate and Isoborneol for the fragrance industry. Further opportunity presents in manufacture and sale of derivatives of these intermediate products. In Synthetic Resin business: increase range of terpene phenols to cater wide needs of customers in domestic market; pursue product approvals with global tyre and adhesive export market; understand customer pain points and provide tailor-made products; introduce wide range of quality products to enable registration with key distributors; explore opportunities of import substitution in adhesives and printing ink industry; improve quality of products to global standards to unlock export opportunities.

The Company remains committed to its core operations and strategic direction. The Board considers it desirable to enhance the borrowing powers for funding capital expenditure, working capital requirements, expansion plans, strategic investments, refinancing of existing borrowings and other general corporate purposes.

Global growth projected to slow from 2.9% in 2025 to 2.5% in 2026; EMDE growth to decelerate to 3.6% in 2026. Industrial metal prices expected to increase ~18% in 2026 on tighter supply and firm demand including from energy transition.

India's chemical industry is expected to remain one of the fastest-growing chemical markets globally, supported by robust domestic demand, favourable government policies, expanding manufacturing capabilities and increasing integration into global supply chains. Industry estimates indicate that the sector is poised to grow at a CAGR of 8–9%, with the market size expected to increase from US$155–165 billion to approximately US$250-300 billion by 2030.

The global chemical industry is expected to remain in a moderate growth phase during FY 2026–27 and beyond, with gradual improvement in demand conditions but continued structural challenges. Growth is projected to remain in the range of 2.5%–3.5% annually, driven primarily by emerging markets in Asia.
The global pine chemicals market is valued at approximately USD 6.7 billion in 2026 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.0%–4.5% through 2034.

The global terpenes market was valued at approximately USD 790 million in 2025 and estimated to reach approximately USD 800 million in 2026 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of around 6.5% through 2035.
The global synthetic resins market was valued at approximately USD 541.8 billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 568.5 billion in 2026, projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.92% through 2033.
The global aroma chemicals market reached approximately USD 7.7 billion in 2025 and forecast to reach USD 12.0 Billion by 2034, implying a CAGR of approximately 4.9%.

The India Aroma Chemicals Market is demonstrating robust growth, poised to significantly expand from its valuation of $291.3 million in 2025 at a CAGR of 5.54% through 2034, reaching an estimated market size of approximately $472.6 million.

The Company enters FY 2026-27 with a positive outlook, supported by improving industry fundamentals, a diversified product portfolio and a strong focus on operational excellence. Strategic priorities include enhancing manufacturing capabilities, strengthening product portfolio through innovation, expanding domestic and global presence, driving sustainable growth, and achieving operational excellence.

The Company will continue to monitor further notifications, amendments and clarifications issued by the appropriate authorities and will recognise the impact, if any, in the period in which such changes become effective.

Raw Material Cost and Supply Risk: Fluctuations in prices and availability of key raw materials, intermediates and chemicals; supply disruptions or procurement cost increases could impact operations and margins.

Regulatory and Compliance Risk: Highly regulated industry subject to environmental, health, safety and chemical handling regulations; changes may increase operational costs and necessitate additional investments.

Market and Competitive Risk: Highly competitive chemical industry with domestic and international players; intense competition, pricing pressure and changing customer preferences may affect market position and profitability.

Demand Risk: Demand for camphor and related products influenced by consumer consumption patterns, festive demand, industrial applications and economic conditions; adverse changes may impact sales volumes and revenue.
Foreign Exchange Risk: Exposure to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates from imports, exports and international transactions, affecting profitability and cash flows.

Supply Chain and Logistics Risk: Disruptions in transportation networks, port operations, shipping availability or global supply chains may impact timely procurement of raw materials and delivery of finished products.

Operational and Manufacturing Risk: Risks related to equipment breakdown, process disruptions, fire incidents, industrial accidents and unplanned shutdowns affecting production and financial performance.
Environmental, Health and Safety Risk: Chemical manufacturing involves hazardous substances; failure to maintain safety systems may result in accidents, regulatory actions and reputational impact.

Geopolitical and Macroeconomic Risk: Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments, inflationary pressures and trade-related restrictions may affect input costs, supply chains and overall business performance.
